key_insight: Adaptive, LLM-guided resource allocation in batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization can better balance exploration and exploitation for materials discovery under changing campaign constraints.
engineering_relevance: This work can help self-driving labs and alloy design pipelines spend limited synthesis and characterization resources more effectively while still improving Pareto-optimal material candidates.
method: Compare exploitation-only, fixed mixed, and two LLM-based adaptive allocation policies.
Apply batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization to alloy design under resource constraints.
Test robustness under baseline, budget-cut, timeline-cut, and combined disruption scenarios.
evidence_signal: Across two alloy systems, mixed and adaptive strategies achieved substantially more mutual information than exploitation-only, with adaptive policies outperforming fixed mixed allocation while maintaining favorable hypervolume and optimization speed tradeoffs.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality of campaign-state interpretation and policy tuning, so performance may vary when transferred to different materials systems or lab workflows.
paper_title: Agentic Resource Allocation for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Autonomous Materials Discovery
